title: Deterministic per-request metering with idempotency tokens and failover-proof accounting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated capacity customers are exposed to occasional duplicate metering events when requests are retried across frontends, when runtime workers are preempted, or during leader failovers. These duplicates cause billing noise, customer disputes, and inaccurate SLA credit calculations.

Goal: Implement a deterministic, low-latency metering scheme that makes every billable request provably idempotent across retries and failovers, while still supporting high-throughput paths for dedicated pools. The system must provide:
- Per-request canonical identifiers and commit semantics that avoid double-billing.
- A lightweight proof-of-commit that can be surfaced to downstream billing and dispute workflows.
- Integration with existing SLA crediting so that missing/failed commit windows can automatically trigger credits where appropriate.

Proposed approach (high level):
1) Request-level idempotency token: require/accept an Idempotency-Token header generated by the gateway or SDK. If absent, gateway will synthesize one from request fingerprint + monotonic counter.
2) Local fast-path commit: worker emits a local commit record (in memory) and responds quickly. The response includes a meter_proof referencing worker-local sequence + token.
3) Durable consensus layer: a background writer batches commit records to an append-only event log (event-sourced ledger) per tenant/pool. Each batch is assigned a ledger sequence and checksum.
4) Reconciliation and dedup: ledger deduplicates by idempotency token during commit ingestion; this ensures eventual canonicalization. Charging and SLA windows rely on the committed ledger sequence numbers rather than transient local counts.
5) Failover semantics: on worker preemption, the gateway/allocator will not reissue the client request if a commit_proof for the token exists in the ledger; if missing, the request can be retried but dedup will prevent double-billing.
6) SLA credit mapping: compute request commit latency by comparing request arrival timestamp to ledger commit timestamp. Commit latency beyond the SLA window produces a credit event linked to the original token.

Trade-offs and constraints: 
- Write amplification and storage: the ledger increases writes and storage per commit; mitigations: time-windowed batching, compression, and TTL for per-request metadata after billing-finalization.
- Increased end-to-end latency for strongly consistent billing guarantees: we choose an optimistic fast-path with async durable commit to keep p99 latency low for callers.
- Complexity: changes span gateway, runtime, ledger ingestion service, billing pipeline, and dashboards. Rollout must be gated behind feature flags.

Required changes (non-exhaustive):
- API: accept optional Idempotency-Token header; SDKs updated to surface token generation.
- Runtime: attach token and local sequence to meter events; surface meter_proof in API response metadata.
- Ledger service: new append-only per-tenant ledger with dedup index on token; batch ingestion endpoint.
- Billing: change downstream billing job to read ledger-sequences instead of worker counters; add crediting logic based on commit latency.
- Observability: new metrics (uncommitted_count, commit_latency_histogram, dedup_hits, ledger_lag) and dashboards.
- Tests: unit, integration, and chaos tests that simulate lost ACKs, network partitions, retries, and preemptions.

Acceptance criteria:
- No observed duplicate billing for synthetic retry scenarios (see e2e tests).
- Ledger dedup reduces duplicate-charge incidents in staging to 0 over a 72-hour fault-injection run.
- Metric dashboards reflect commit latency and ledger lag; SLA credit automation is exercised by tests.
- SDKs and gateway produce and propagate Idempotency-Token for downstream telemetry.

Dependencies: ENG-40123 (metering refactor to normalize worker counters) and ENG-33011 (subsecond ledger prototype) are helpful but not blockers.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Feature-flagged deploy of Idempotency-Token generation in gateway + SDK release.
2) Deploy runtime fast-path changes to a small canary pool.
3) Run ledger in read-only ingest mode while comparing worker counters vs ledger dedup results to validate parity.
4) Switch billing ingestion to ledger sequences behind a flag; monitor for divergence.
5) Full rollout and enable automated SLA crediting.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: dedup index growth causing memory pressure. Mitigation: TTL + compaction + bounded in-memory cache with fallback to on-disk store.
- Risk: long-lived races during rollout. Mitigation: dual-writing mode + reconciliation reports + short canaries.

Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Deterministic+Metering+Design
- Ledger prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128
- Billing pipeline spike: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBilledSpikeExample
acceptance_criteria: Requests must be idempotent across retries and failovers: synthetic retry test shows zero duplicate charges
Ledger dedup removes >99.99% of duplicate meter events during 72h chaos run
Billing pipeline consumes ledger sequences and crediting automates for commits outside SLA window
New metrics and dashboards available in Console; alerting set for ledger_lag > 10s
comments: 2026-01-21 - Kickoff: scoping call with runtime, billing, and gateway. Agreed to pursue optimistic fast-path + async ledger commit.

2026-01-28 - Design review: PM (Evan Li) requested clearer owner semantics for token generation in the SDK vs gateway. Action: gateway will synthesize token when absent; SDK will prefer client-supplied tokens.
2026-02-05 - Security review queue: encryption-at-rest for ledger and access controls required. Sec team (Marina Cortez) requested ACLs on per-tenant ledger endpoints. Added to tasks.
2026-02-17 - Proto PR opened for fast-path proof header: runtime PR #4128. Linked above. Initial perf shows 1.8% p99 increase when including proof header; acceptable for P0 customers.

2026-02-28 - Billing spike complete: new billing job can read ledger sequences but we discovered a clock-skew edge where commit_latency computed negative. Added normalization by using gateway arrival timestamp embedded in record.
2026-03-07 - QA: chaos test failing intermittently when ledger compaction runs during heavy ingestion. Next steps: add backpressure to ingestion and retry with backoff.
